assessment.status_reason: A shortlist can be justified: MIR-ATR suits a melt in contact with a crystal, and a shown application reports MIR-ATR spectra of API in hot polymer during extrusion. What is not covered by any supplied source is whether a probe survives the hot interface and build-up, so the plan rests on the stated assumptions and on the open questions.

premise_checks.premise: An optical probe at the process interface can detect composition changes in a hot polymer melt in-line.
premise_checks.explanation: A conference slide shows MIR-ATR spectra of API in hot polymer obtained during extrusion, which is a reason to test the method here, not proof that it will work for this process.

citations.quote: Spectra of API in hot polymer obtained with Diamond cone ATR probe coupled to iC10 FTIR (MTAC)

premise_checks.premise: A probe exposed to a hot interface that may build up material can keep measuring reliably.
premise_checks.explanation: No supplied source addresses fouling, cleaning or probe ratings for a hot polymer melt; the shallow ATR sampling depth makes the concern real, but the mitigation is not described anywhere in the material.

requirements_stated: Compare optical methods for detecting composition changes in a hot polymer melt carrying an active pharmaceutical ingredient.
Provide the questions that must be answered before a probe is chosen.
The process interface is hot and may be exposed to material build-up.
Offline assays are available as a reference.
key_unknowns: Identity of the API and the concentration range over which composition change must be seen.
Optical behaviour of the melt: transparent, strongly scattering or opaque, and presence of fillers or additives.
Whether the API or the polymer fluoresces, which decides the Raman option.
Melt temperature and pressure at the intended measurement point.
Installation point, access and distance from the port to the spectrometer.
Required accuracy and response time, and the uncertainty of the existing offline assay.

clarification_questions.question: Is the melt at the measurement point transparent, strongly scattering or opaque, and does it contain fillers, pigments or other particulates?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The optical behaviour decides whether a reflection or a transmission geometry is meaningful at all, and therefore whether the NIR reflection comparison applies.

clarification_questions.question: Which active pharmaceutical ingredient is used, and over what concentration range must a composition change be detected?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The identity and level of the API decide which method has usable bands and whether the target sits below the sensitivity of a method.

clarification_questions.question: What are the melt temperature and pressure at the intended measurement point?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Both set what the probe, crystal and fiber must tolerate and whether an in-line port is feasible at that location.

clarification_questions.question: Where is the measurement point, how far is it from the spectrometer, and how often can a probe be accessed for cleaning?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Access and distance fix the probe geometry and the fiber link, and build-up at the port cannot be managed without access.

clarification_questions.question: Do the polymer or the API fluoresce under visible or near-infrared laser light?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: A strong fluorescence background can swamp the Raman bands and would decide against the Raman comparison.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy and response time must the measurement reach, and how uncertain is the existing offline assay?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The go/no-go threshold and the usable reference both come from these numbers, and without them no method can be judged adequate.

recommendations.rationale: ATR fiber probes handle liquids and soft solids in contact with the crystal, and a shown application reports MIR-ATR spectra of API in hot polymer during extrusion. Mid-IR gives well-defined absorption bands, which is the most direct route to an API fingerprint inside a polymer matrix.
recommendations.conditions: Applies if the melt wets the ATR crystal and the API has a mid-IR band that is not buried by the polymer matrix.

citations.quote: Spectra of API in hot polymer obtained with Diamond cone ATR probe coupled to iC10 FTIR (MTAC)
ATR fiber probes (Fig.1) enable the analysis of liquids and solid elastic samples
Vibrational spectroscopy in the mid-IR range (4000-400 cm-1) is one of the most informative methods of chemical analysis.

recommendations.rationale: Mid-IR and Raman spectra are complementary, and Raman reports the molecular backbone and symmetrical non-polar groups, so it is the natural second single-method test on the same samples. Running it as its own method, not fused, shows whether it adds anything the mid-IR spectrum misses.
recommendations.conditions: Worth keeping only if fluorescence from the polymer or the API does not swamp the Raman bands on real melt samples.

citations.quote: This property makes mid-IR and Raman spectra complementary, that is, they complement each other.
Raman provides information on the molecular backbone and symmetrical non-polar groups.

recommendations.rationale: A shown extrusion application pairs NIR reflection with MIR-ATR for in-line control, so NIR reflection is the expected alternative to check. It is only sensible if the melt scatters strongly, since reflection is less representative for clear liquids.
recommendations.conditions: Only if the melt is opaque or strongly scattering and a reflection probe can be mounted at the port, which is decided by the answer on optical behaviour.

citations.quote: NIR-Reflex & MIR-ATR-spectroscopy to control polymer extrusion in-line
reflection can work well in highly scattering environments but can be less representative for clear liquids.

measurement_concept.probe_and_geometry: First choice is an ATR fiber probe in contact with the melt, mounted at a port in the extruder or die adaptor; Raman would use a separate contact probe on the same port or a neighbouring one, NIR reflection a non-contact probe if the melt is strongly scattering.
measurement_concept.location: A single, well-flushed measurement point where the melt is homogeneous, not in a dead zone where build-up would collect.
measurement_concept.fiber_link: The fiber family follows the method: mid-IR needs chalcogenide or polycrystalline infrared fibers, Raman needs silica fibers free of polymer-jacket fluorescence; the achievable link length for a mid-IR probe at a production extruder is not stated in the supplied material.

citations.quote: Free of Polymer jacket fluorescence for Raman and Fluo- Spectroscopy

spectral_ranges.statement: Nominal mid-IR range 4000-400 cm-1; the usable range depends on the fiber, crystal and spectrometer actually selected.

citations.quote: Vibrational spectroscopy in the mid-IR range (4000-400 cm-1)

spectral_ranges.statement: Raman is reported as Raman shift in cm-1, with the laser excitation wavelength stated separately; neither value is fixed for this case yet.

citations.quote: The Raman shift is used as the horizontal (spectral) axis in Raman spectroscopy

spectral_ranges.statement: Nominal NIR range 780-2500 nm; the usable range depends on the instrument, fiber and probe actually selected.

citations.quote: NIR spectra (780-2500 nm) contain predominantly overtones and component bands of fundamental vibrations

risks.risk: Build-up on the ATR crystal can make the measurement unrepresentative, because ATR samples only a surface layer a few micrometres deep.

citations.quote: typically at a depth of few microns

risks.risk: The API bands may be hidden by the polymer matrix in mid-IR, or by polymer fluorescence in Raman, once real melt samples are measured.
The melt temperature and pressure at the probe may exceed what a probe and fiber can tolerate, and no supplied source gives ratings for a hot melt.
If the required accuracy is tighter than the method can reach, or the API level is a trace component, no option in this shortlist meets the target.

steps.step: Collect melt samples or process states that span the expected API range, the polymer grades and the melt temperatures, including start-up and any known off-spec material.
steps.purpose: Cover the chemical and physical variation the method must survive.

citations.quote: Representative samples or process states

steps.step: Record MIR-ATR spectra of each sample at process-representative temperature, then Raman spectra on the same material, keeping each method as its own single-method data set.
steps.purpose: Single methods first, so each can be judged on its own before any combination is considered.

steps.step: Obtain an independent reference value for every sample from the customer's existing offline assay, measured on the same material.
steps.purpose: Give the calibration an independent reference and define what is compared.

citations.quote: independent reference measurements, what is compared, and the basis for the go / no-go decision.

steps.step: Build and validate one calibration per method on held-out runs or batches, and repeat a reference-standard check before and after a run to see whether build-up shifts the signal.
steps.purpose: Separate real composition change from drift caused by the interface.

steps.step: Fix the go/no-go threshold from the customer's required accuracy and response time before the trials, and drop any method that does not reach it.
steps.purpose: Make the decision on the customer's numbers, not on the spectra looking plausible.

feasibility_plan.reference_measurements: The customer's existing offline assay, run on the same material as the spectra.
feasibility_plan.decision_basis: Go if one method reaches the customer's required accuracy and response time on held-out runs; no-go otherwise.

assumptions: The melt is hot enough to flow but remains in contact with an ATR crystal without degrading it.
The API has at least one absorption band that is not fully overlapped by the polymer matrix.
The existing offline assay is accurate enough to serve as the calibration reference.

assessment.chemometrics_note: A quantitative answer needs one calibration per method, built on the customer's offline assay values. Calibration is specific to the matrix, so the model has to be re-validated when the polymer grade, the additives or the API range changes.
assessment.realtime_tracking_note: The aim is continuous tracking of the melt while it is processed. Acquisition rate and averaging must match the required response time, which is not yet known.
assessment.future_direction: Once one method meets the targets, a compact analyser dedicated to that single measurement point would be the later step, rather than a full multi-method system.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the API bands are buried by the polymer in mid-IR, or polymer fluorescence swamps Raman, the choice moves to the NIR reflection comparison (M3). If the melt temperature, the pressure or the build-up at the port proves unmanageable, the installation concept has to change before any method is fixed.
proposal.next_step: Answer the questions on API and range, melt conditions and optical behaviour, and supply representative melt samples with their offline assay values so the first single-method comparison can be run.

assessment.brief_answer: Test mid-infrared ATR first: a shown application reports MIR-ATR spectra of API in hot polymer during extrusion, and ATR suits a melt in contact with a crystal. Raman is the natural second single-method test on the same samples; NIR reflection only if the melt proves strongly scattering. Still open: the API and its concentration range, the melt temperature and access at the port, and how build-up will be managed.
